title: Acceptance criteria and scope: Minimal viable promptset & progressive rollback for Optimize
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD-level acceptance criteria and scope clarification for a Minimal Viable Promptset (MVP-set) and a progressive rollback policy for Redwood Optimize evals. Goal: enable safe, measurable rollouts of optimizer recommendations (quantization, batching, model swap) with clear gating for A/B and canary experiments using small, high-fidelity prompt cohorts plus lightweight random-sample coverage of production traffic.
background: Optimize needs a defendable, low-friction evaluation contract that balances statistical confidence with operational cost. Existing docs define guardrails for broad eval strategy; this ticket defines the light-weight promptset composition, the minimum sample counts, per-cohort thresholds, severity weighting for regressions, and the progressive rollback schedule used by the Console and Runtime to automatically throttle or revert changes.
scope_inclusions: Definition of Minimal Viable Promptset (MVP-set) composition: high-priority cohorts + long-tail sparse samples
Quantified acceptance criteria for canary and A/B experiments (per-cohort thresholds and statistical tests)
A progressive rollback policy that maps signal thresholds to traffic reduction steps and automatic fallback to nominated safe model variants
Instrumenting signals and dashboards required to evaluate acceptance criteria
Runbook text for automated alerts and manual ops intervention points
scope_exclusions: Full-scale stratified census sampling (deferred to follow-up PRD)
Changes to runtime kernel selection heuristics (engineering spike required separately)
New model onboarding workflow for external partner models
acceptance_criteria: MVP-set size and composition defined: 6 targeted cohorts (two high-volume cohorts, two safety/guardrail cohorts, two long-tail representative cohorts) plus a 0.5% random sample of live traffic for approx 1k tokens/day baseline
Per-cohort primary metric (accuracy/QA score/semantic-similarity depending on cohort) baseline calculated over a 14-day rolling window and stored in Optimize eval store
Statistical gating specified: two-sided sequential t-test with alpha=0.01 and minimum 200 effective samples per cohort for a valid signal (exceptions documented for low-volume cohorts)
Severity-weighted regression scoring defined: each cohort assigned severity weight (3 high, 2 medium, 1 low); acceptance requires composite score delta <= 0.03 absolute or p>=0.01
Canary rollout plan encoded: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% traffic steps with hold windows (24h for first two steps, 48h after 20%) and automated health checks
Automated rollback rules implemented: immediate rollback on any cohort with absolute primary-metric regression > 5% and p<0.01 OR composite severity-weighted regression exceeding 0.06
A/B criteria include minimum experiment duration of 48 hours, at least 5k unique requests per variant, and pre-registered primary/secondary metrics in the Console
Dashboard widgets and alerting exist for per-cohort sample counts, baseline drift, effect size, p-value, and composite severity score
End-to-end test harness exercise (PR-based) that can simulate canary steps with synthetic prompt traffic and verify rollback triggers
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Dry-run in Optimize sandbox using MVP promptset and synthetic traffic (owners: PM + Eng test harness)
Stage 1: Internal canary against 1% traffic for 24h; if no alert, advance to 5% for 24h
Stage 2: 20% for 48h with full monitoring enabled; if composite score stable, proceed to 50% and then 100%
At each step, a manual thumbs-up gate exists for a human-in-the-loop override (SRE/PM + product owner)
If rollback trigger fires, traffic is reduced according to progressive rollback policy (see rollback_triggers) and an incident runbook is invoked
monitoring_signals: Primary metric(s) per cohort (e.g., factuality_score, semantic_similarity, success_rate)
Secondary metrics: latency P95, error rate, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens
Sampling signal: per-cohort sample_count and time-to-first-sample
Operational: model-fallback-rate, KV cache miss rate
regression_thresholds: Per-cohort action thresholds: advisory if delta >= 0.02 absolute; requires manual review if delta >= 0.03 absolute; automatic protective action if delta >= 0.05 absolute AND p<0.01
Composite severity-weighted threshold: score <= 0.03 allowed; 0.03 < score <= 0.06 manual mitigation required; score > 0.06 triggers automated rollback
Latency and error budget: if latency P95 increases by >25% or error rate increases by >0.5 percentage points from baseline during a hold window, pause rollout and investigate
ab_criteria: Experiment registration required prior to traffic assignment in Console with declared primary metric, cohorts, and minimum sample target
Minimum 5k unique requests per variant OR 7 days of experiment runtime (whichever comes first) before declaring significance
Pre-specified alpha=0.01 for primary metric; secondary metrics use alpha=0.05 and are used for annotations not automatic rollback
Sequential testing allowed only with pre-defined spending and alpha correction (alpha spending function configured in the eval runner)
rollback_triggers: Immediate rollback to safe variant if any high-severity cohort shows absolute regression > 5% with p<0.01
Progressive traffic reduction: on medium-severity composite breach, reduce traffic by 50% and observe for 24h; if unresolved, reduce to 10% and then rollback
Automatic fallback to pinned model variant and eviction of experimental quantization profile on rollback
Notify stakeholders and open incident if fallback occurs; attach latest eval report and sample prompts to the incident ticket
open_questions: For low-volume cohorts (expected <200 samples/day) do we accept relaxed minimums (e.g., Bayesian credible interval) or force pooling? Decision required from Research/Applied ML
Do we require per-token cost delta limits for rollout gating (to avoid cost regressions) or keep cost as a secondary metrics only?
What is the nominated safe variant naming convention and how will engineering expose it to the Console UI?
Should we integrate the severity weights into Optimize policy configuration UI or keep them hard-coded in initial MVP?
